chapter_name: Cell: The Building Block of Life
learning_objective: 🎯 Zoom in on life! Discover how tiny microscopic cells function as complex, bustling cities that keep all living organisms alive.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Robert Hooke discovered cells in 1665 while looking at a slice of cork under a primitive microscope. He called them 'cells' because they looked like little empty rooms!

Prokaryotic cells (like bacteria) are simple and have no defined nucleus; their DNA floats freely. Eukaryotic cells (like plants and animals) are complex and have a true nucleus surrounded by a membrane.
The Nucleus is the 'Brain' holding DNA. Mitochondria are the 'Powerhouses' making energy. Ribosomes make proteins. The Lysosomes are the 'Garbage disposals' cleaning up waste.

Plant cells have a tough rigid Cell Wall (for support), large central Vacuoles (for water storage), and Chloroplasts (for photosynthesis). Animal cells do not have cell walls or chloroplasts, and their vacuoles are small.
Cells breathe and drink! Diffusion is the movement of gases (like Oxygen) from high to low concentration. Osmosis is the specific movement of WATER across the cell membrane to balance concentrations.

fun_activity.title: 🥚 The Naked Egg Experiment
fun_activity.instructions: Soak a raw egg in vinegar for 24 hours. The acid dissolves the hard shell, leaving only the soft cell membrane! You now have a giant, squishy 'naked cell'. If you put it in pure water, it will swell up due to Osmosis!

exam_tips: 📌 Be ready to draw and label a Plant Cell and an Animal Cell. Highlighting the 3 main differences (Wall, Chloroplast, Large Vacuole) is a guaranteed question.
📌 Know the 'Powerhouse' (Mitochondria) and the 'Suicide Bags' (Lysosomes) by their nicknames and functions.
📌 Remember that the Plasma Membrane is 'selectively permeable'—it chooses what gets to come in and go out.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Cell Theory states: All living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and all cells come from pre-existing cells.
⭐ DNA is found inside the nucleus packaged into structures called chromosomes.
⭐ Only plant cells can make their own food using sunlight, thanks to chlorophyll inside their chloroplasts.
